title: Chicken and Dumplings
subtitle: Tender chicken in a thick broth with soft dropped dumplings
excerpt: Boneless chicken thighs simmered in a rich vegetable broth with pillowy dropped dumplings cooked directly in the pot. The Southern American version uses soft, thick dumplings rather than rolled ones.
sourceNotes: Southern American comfort food. The dropped dumpling style is the most common American version; rolled flat dumplings are a variation from further south.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The chicken broth can be made a day ahead and refrigerated. Add the dumpling batter and cook fresh just before serving.

content.text: Chicken and dumplings is a thick, stew-like dish where soft dumplings cook directly in the broth. The lid must stay on while the dumplings steam or they will turn heavy. Do not stir once the dumplings go in.
Melt the butter in the dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery. Cook for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and plain flour. Stir for 1 minute until the flour smells cooked.
Pour in the chicken stock. Add the thyme and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken chunks. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the broth has thickened slightly.

Make the dumplings: rub the cold butter into the self-raising flour and salt until the mix looks like breadcrumbs. Pour in the cold milk and stir briefly until a shaggy dough just comes together. Do not overmix.
Remove the thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Drop tablespoons of the dumpling dough onto the surface of the simmering broth. Leave space between them as they will puff up.
Cover with a tight lid. Cook for 15 minutes without lifting the lid. The dumplings are done when they have puffed and feel set on top. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The dumplings are dense and heavy.
items.cause: The dough was overmixed, or the lid was lifted during cooking.
items.fix: Mix until the dough just comes together, no more. Keep the lid firmly on for the full 15 minutes.

items.symptom: The dumplings are doughy in the centre.
items.cause: The broth was not at a steady simmer when they went in.
items.fix: Make sure the broth is simmering before adding the dumplings. Test one by tearing it in half; the inside should look fluffy and dry.

items.cause: Not enough flour was used to thicken it, or it was not simmered long enough.
items.fix: Simmer the broth for an extra 5 minutes before adding the dumplings to help it reduce and thicken.
